Item status from consensus and stability

Source: R/status.R
delphi_status.Rd

Combines delphi_consensus() and delphi_stability() to classify every item at a given round, and flags the items to submit again in the next round.

Usage

delphi_status(
  x,
  round = NULL,
  threshold = 0.2,
  relative_to = c("points", "range"),
  method = c("wilcoxon", "scheibe", "both"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  scheibe = 0.15,
  type = 7,
  paired = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object.

round

Round to assess, for each indicator. NULL (default) uses the last round of each indicator. Stability is measured between this round and the previous one.

threshold, relative_to

Consensus rule, see delphi_consensus().

method, alpha, scheibe, paired

Stability rule, see delphi_stability().

type

Quantile algorithm; see delphi_describe().

Value

A data frame of class delphi_status with columns indicator, item, round, median, iqr, consensus, stable, status and next_round.

Details

Each item gets one of four statuses:

statusconsensusstablenext round
"consensus"yesyesno
"unstable consensus"yesnoyes
"stable dissent"noyesno
"open"nonoyes

A stable dissent means that opinions have stopped moving without converging: another round is unlikely to produce consensus, and the disagreement is itself a result to report. When only one round is available, stability cannot be assessed (stable = NA); items with consensus are then "consensus" and the others "open".

Examples

x <- delphi_data(delphi_example, expert_col = "expert",
                 round_col = "round", indicator_col = "indicator",
                 scale = list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100)))
st <- delphi_status(x)
st
#>     indicator item round median iqr consensus stable             status
#>        impact   E1     2      8   1      TRUE   TRUE          consensus

#>        impact   E5     2      4   7     FALSE   TRUE     stable dissent
#>        impact   E6     2      3   2      TRUE   TRUE          consensus

#>        impact   E8     2      5   2      TRUE   TRUE          consensus
#>  plausibility   E1     2     78  11      TRUE   TRUE          consensus
#>  plausibility   E2     2     30   8      TRUE   TRUE          consensus
#>  plausibility   E3     2     60  15      TRUE   TRUE          consensus

#>  plausibility   E6     2     30  16      TRUE   TRUE          consensus
#>  plausibility   E7     2     83  11      TRUE  FALSE unstable consensus
#>  plausibility   E8     2     41  24     FALSE   TRUE     stable dissent

#>       FALSE

# Items to submit again in the next round
subset(st, next_round)
